# Implementation-Ready Architecture Research: FastAPI Photo Editor Moving Beyond 8-bit Pillow + Global Histogram Heuristics

Scope: near-final, natural photographic edits (exposure, white balance, tone curve, vibrance/saturation, style look) comparable in *kind* to a Lightroom develop module — not a claim of Lightroom parity. No model below is asserted to match Lightroom output without matched A/B testing on your own holdout.

---

## 0. Top candidate recommendations (evidence-graded)

| # | Component | Candidate | License status | Evidence vs. proposal |
|---|-----------|-----------|----------------|----------------------|
| 1 | Core edit engine | **Image-Adaptive 3D LUT (Zeng et al., TPAMI 2022)** or **LUTwithBGrid (ECCV 2024)** | Apache-2.0 code [1] [2] | *Evidence*: <600K params, <2 ms for 4K on one Titan RTX, and a model trained at 480p transfers to 4K+ with no performance drop [1]. *Proposal*: use as your primary retouching engine, retrained on data you have rights to (see §1). |
| 2 | Style/look system | **NILUT (AAAI 2024)** — neural implicit 3D LUTs, MIT-licensed code; fits existing professional .cube LUTs from Hald images in <30 s [3] [4] | Code MIT; its .cube LUT data CC 4.0; underlying MIT5K images keep the original Adobe research license [3] | *Evidence*: pixel-wise-only transform ⇒ "no artifacts are introduced"; compact vs. full 3D LUTs [4]. *Proposal*: adopt for user-installable looks; do not train on its bundled MIT5K-derived image data commercially. |
| 3 | Spatially varying engine (phase 2) | **HDRNet bilateral grid (Gharbi et al., SIGGRAPH 2017)** | Code Apache-2.0 [5] | *Evidence*: 12 MP 16-bit input in 61 ms; full-resolution training loss handles non-scale-invariant operators [6]. *Proposal*: introduce only after the LUT engine, because the reference implementation is archived and TF1-era. |
| 4 | Restoration (optional, opt-in) | **NAFNet** (MIT code [7]), **Real-ESRGAN** (BSD-3-Clause code & weights [8]), **Restormer** (code MIT per repo metadata; paper CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 — see §4) | | *Evidence*: NAFNet-SIDD-width64 40.30 dB PSNR on SIDD denoising [9]. *Proposal*: opt-in pre-processing only; restoration edits add texture and can violate "near-final natural edit" intent (§4). |
| 5 | RAW decode / color management | **rawpy (LibRaw wrapper), MIT**, 16-bit linear output, LCMS engine bundled [10] | MIT (LibRaw is LGPL-2.1); GPL demosaic packs excluded from wheels [11] | *Evidence*: `raw.postprocess(gamma=(1,1), no_auto_bright=True, output_bps=16)` [12]. *Proposal*: replace the 8-bit Pillow path with rawpy 16-bit linear → linear Rec.2020/scene-linear working space → learned model → display transform. |

---

## 1. Datasets: licensing and training suitability

### 1.1 MIT-Adobe FiveK — **NOT MIT-licensed; research-only**
Despite the "MIT FiveK" name, the images are governed by a **Research License from Adobe Systems and MIT**, not an MIT open-source license. The license text permits use "solely for your own research purposes" and forbids use "intended for or directed toward commercial advantage or monetary compensation"; it also bars using Adobe/MIT names for endorsement, requires copyright notices, terminates on breach, and ships AS-IS with no warranty [13].

**Consequence for your product:** you may *evaluate and prototype* on FiveK internally, but you may **not train a production model on FiveK pairs for a commercial photo editor** without separate written permission from Adobe. This is the single largest licensing blocker in the plan. Note also that NILUT's MIT5K-derived dataset (13 GB, 100 images processed with professional 3D LUTs in Lightroom) explicitly "keeps the original license" of the FiveK images [3] — the MIT code license does not launder the data license.

### 1.2 PPR10K — **non-commercial research only**
11,161 high-quality RAW portrait photos (4K–8K) in 1,681 groups, each retouched by three expert retouchers, with full-resolution human-region masks, XMP CameraRaw metadata for source and all three targets, and pretrained models (12 .pth files) [14] [15]. The dataset files are "available for non-commercial research purposes only"; no reproduction, resale, or commercial exploitation of the images **or derived data**; repo *code* is Apache-2.0 [16]. Its XMP target files are especially interesting architecturally (expert Lightroom parameter edits, not just pixels), and a derived instruction-following dataset (MMArt-PPR10k, 350k rows with before/after images plus Lightroom Lua/XMP configs) lists apache-2.0 on Hugging Face — but the page does not state the upstream PPR10K license, so upstream non-commercial terms still govern the underlying photos [17]. The paper also states models trained on general (non-portrait) retouching data "can hardly meet" portrait requirements — so PPR10K-style behavior cannot be substituted by FiveK-trained models [15].

**Consequence:** PPR10K is a research/eval asset only. For a commercial portrait mode you need licensed portraits of your own (or commissioned retouching pairs), using PPR10K's recipes (HRP loss, GLC) as methodology, not its pixels.

### 1.3 Google HDR+ Burst Photography Dataset — **CC BY-SA 4.0**
3,640 bursts / 28,461 RAW images from Android cameras (Nexus/Pixel, 12–13 MP), DNG + sidecar color metadata (lens shading maps, rgb2rgb sensor matrix, AsShotNeutral WB gains), merged.dng and final.jpg outputs; "broad and largely unencumbered," intended for scientific purposes, with a good-taste caveat since subjects are the authors' friends and family [18].

**Consequence:** usable commercially in principle (CC BY-SA with attribution + share-alike on derivatives — have counsel confirm share-alike handling for model weights trained on it). But it is a *burst/denoising/HDR-merge* dataset, not expert-retouching pairs; it trains restoration/merging behavior, not Lightroom-style tone/look editing [18].

### 1.4 SIDD — **MIT-licensed dataset and code**
~30,000 noisy real smartphone images (10 scenes, five phones incl. low/normal/high exposure conditions), MIT License for the dataset and associated repositories; SIDD-Small (160 pairs) explicitly "can be used for training/learning purposes"; includes DNG metadata and a reference MATLAB camera pipeline for raw→sRGB rendering [19]. A revised "SIDD with more accurate colors" (SIDD-CC) exists — prefer it where color fidelity matters [19].

### 1.5 Licensing unknowns to resolve before training
- **FiveK**: no commercial training path in the license; contact Adobe for a data license if FiveK-style expert targets are essential [13].
- **PPR10K**: no commercial path; XMP/derived-data restrictions; contact liang27jie@gmail.com [16].
- **HDR+ weights question**: CC BY-SA 4.0 "share-alike" applicability to trained model weights is untested; obtain counsel opinion [18].
- **Restormer weights**: paper is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 [20]; code repo metadata says MIT (§4) — verify the LICENSE file yourself before shipping.
- **EHNQ night-image database**: no stated license on the IEEE page [21].
- **KonIQ-10k**: images are YFCC100M entries under CC licenses allowing editing/redistribution, described as "freely available to the research community," but no single explicit license type is named on the official page — confirm per-image CC terms [22] [23].

---

## 2. Production learned retouching

### 2.1 Bilateral grids / HDRNet
HDRNet predicts locally-affine color coefficients in a bilateral grid from a low-res (256×256) input and applies them at full resolution via a learned slicing node, with the **loss evaluated at full resolution** during training — this is what gives resolution-consistent output and captures high-frequency, non-scale-invariant operator behavior [6]. Measured: 12 MP 16-bit input in 61 ms (vs 400–600 ms reference), 1080p in 14 ms on a Pixel phone; grid of 16×16×8 with 3×4 affine transforms (96 channels) [6].

Production caveats from the official repo: **the repo was archived June 12, 2024 (read-only)**; `BilateralSliceApply` is GPU-only with no CPU implementation planned; shipped pretrained models may differ from the paper's evaluation models; the HDR+ pretrained model expects specially formatted 16-bit linear input and running it on sRGB "may produce uncanny colors"; stack is Python 2.7 / TF-custom-op era; "not an official Google product" [5]. A PyTorch reimplementation (HDRnet-PyTorch, MIT) exists but shows limited maintenance (53 stars, fixed architecture, slow CPU data pipeline) [24]. The paper also scopes the method to photographic enhancements that **do not warp the image or add new edges** — i.e., tone/color edits, not restoration [6].

### 2.2 Adaptive 3D LUTs
- **Image-Adaptive 3D LUT (Zeng et al., TPAMI 2022)**: small CNN predicts weights to fuse basis 3D LUTs; <600K params, <2 ms on 4K (Titan RTX); trained at 480p, applied at 4K+ with no performance drop; Apache-2.0; includes paired and unpaired training scripts, identity-LUT generation, C++/CUDA trilinear interpolation, and local tone mapping code [1].
- **LUTwithBGrid (ECCV 2024)**: combines bilateral grids with adaptive 3D LUTs, adding spatial information to the color transform via slicing while keeping real-time inference; Apache-2.0 with pretrained models for FiveK and PPR10K protocols; requires compiled C++/CUDA extensions [2].
- **SVDLUT (ICCV 2025)**: decomposes spatial-aware 3D LUTs via SVD into low-dimensional LUTs for parameter/runtime savings; Apache-2.0, pretrained FiveK/PPR10K models; explicitly motivated by spatial modules whose cost grows "particularly as the resolution of the input image rises" — the current resolution-scaling concern in this family [25].
- **PPR10K's retouching model** is itself built on Image-Adaptive-3DLUT with a CUDA trilinear implementation, plus Human-Region Priority and Group-Level Consistency training strategies — reuse the recipes [14].

### 2.3 NILUT and implicit LUTs
NILUT (AAAI 2024) parameterizes a continuous 3D color transform with a small network: emulates real 3D LUTs accurately, encodes multiple styles with implicit blending, memory-efficient and differentiable, pluggable into learned ISPs; fitting a professional .cube LUT via a Hald image takes <30 s (`fit.py --steps 1000 --units 128 --layers 2`) [3] [4]. Being strictly pixel-wise, "no artifacts are introduced"; a pretrained `nilutx3style.pt` encodes three styles [3]. Known gaps: the project page marks training code "will be released soon" and style interpolation as in-progress [4] — and, again, its bundled image dataset inherits the FiveK research license [3].

### 2.4 Full-resolution inference consistency — what the evidence supports
- Resolution-invariance is *demonstrated for global/low-capacity operators*: adaptive 3D LUTs trained at 480p apply to 4K+ unchanged [1]; HDRNet's full-resolution training loss exists precisely because low-res-only inference misses high-frequency, non-scale-invariant effects [6].
- A recent retouching study warns that ultra-light global operators (1×1 networks) can satisfy whole-image statistics by regional offsetting — capacity limits show up as under-correction on hard inputs (its model needed a manual luma gain of +5.0 dB on over-exposed inputs) [26].
- For pixel-wise-convolutional restorers at very large sizes, **tiling with overlap + seamless blending** is the practical route: a reference implementation (Apache-2.0) supports linear/Gaussian/multi-band (Laplacian) blending, minimum-energy seam selection, and per-tile histogram matching (Reinhard-style mean/σ transfer) to kill tile color drift; recommended starts: overlap=64, gaussian, strength 0.25, or overlap=128 + multi_band 0.3 for high-contrast content; merge in image space, not latent space [27]. Restormer's official demo likewise ships a "tile option for testing on large images" [28].
- **Proposal (unproven until you test):** run your retouching model on a fixed downsampled pyramid / representative downscale, transfer parameters (LUT weights, bilateral coefficients) to full resolution — the property the 3D-LUT papers report — and validate on a full-resolution holdout across ISO/exposure levels; treat tile-based restoration (not LUT retouching) as the only path needing seam-blending machinery.

### 2.5 Recent alternatives to watch
Beyond the above: CLUT-Net (ACM MM 2022, adaptive LUT compression, cited from the 3DLUT repo) [1]; AdaInt (acknowledged base of SVDLUT) [25]; CSRNet, Zero-DCE, and eLIR-Net named as the efficient global-retouching architecture landscape [26]; the mv-lab AISP repo as an ISP-adjacent resource [3].

---

## 3. Restoration models: licenses and risks

- **NAFNet** (Megvii, ECCV 2022): repo released under the **MIT License** (Copyright 2022 megvii-model), permissive for commercial use; dependency BasicSR is Apache-2.0 (keep notices) [7]. Evidence: 40.30 dB PSNR / 0.9614 SSIM on SIDD denoising (width64), 33.69 dB on GoPro deblurring; pretrained weights on Google Drive/Baidu [9].
- **Restormer** (CVPR 2022 Oral): the arXiv page states "License: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0" for the paper [20]; third-party repo metadata lists the code repo as **MIT** with weights on Google Drive, but the repo is "Stale" (last push ~1 year, 55 open issues) [29] and a fork records a 2025 "MIT License" commit — **verify the LICENSE file in the official swz30/Restormer repo yourself before shipping** [28]. Its transposed-attention gives linear complexity for high-resolution inputs [20].
- **Real-ESRGAN**: code and pretrained weights under the **BSD 3-Clause License** (Copyright 2021 Xintao Wang) — permits commercial use and redistribution with notice retention; no warranty [8].

**Restoration risks for a "near-final natural edit" product:**
1. Restoration changes content, not just tone: denoise/deblur/super-resolution models add, remove, or hallucinate texture. HDRNet's own scoping (tone ops that don't add edges) marks the boundary of "retouching" vs. "restoration" [6].
2. These networks are trained on distortion benchmarks (SIDD, GoPro, REDS), not on retouched-photo aesthetics; none of their pages reports human preference or Lightroom comparisons [9] [29].
3. All three model families are essentially unmaintained (Real-ESRGAN 2021, Restormer "Stale", HDRNet archived June 2024) — plan to own the inference code rather than the repos [5] [29].
4. Tiled large-image inference for restorers reintroduces seam/consistency risk (§2.4) [28] [27].

**Recommendation:** ship LUT/bilateral retouching as the default engine; expose NAFNet-SIDD denoising and Real-ESRGAN upscaling as clearly-labeled opt-in tools, validated per-skin-tone and per-scene before enabling (§4).

---

## 4. Photographic quality evaluation

- **Human preference / technical quality:** KonIQ-10k — 10,073 authentic images, 1.2M crowdsourced ratings from 1,459 workers (~120 per image), MOS + distributions; images are YFCC100M CC-licensed; the KonCept512 no-reference model reaches 0.921 SROCC on KonIQ-10k [22] [23]. It measures technical quality, not aesthetic retouching preference — it cannot by itself establish Lightroom comparability [23].
- **PSNR/SSIM are insufficient for retouching:** whole-frame PSNR/SSIM can stay flat while skin-region chromatic defects appear; a retouching study reports a green skin cast under synthetic self-supervision (skin Δa* −8.3) with near-unchanged whole-frame PSNR/SSIM, and shows global image-mean losses *worsen* it; it recommends signed skin-region Δa* paired with whole-frame metrics and skin-tone-stratified evaluation (dark/medium/light) [26]. Models trained on real FiveK expert pairs stayed near-neutral on skin (Δa* −0.96) — an argument for expert-pair supervision over synthetic degradation [26].
- **Skin tones:** use CIEDE2000 on face ROIs with explicit thresholds — ΔE00 ≈ 1 is a just-noticeable difference, 1–3 good, 3–5 acceptable, >5 clearly visible; validate with Monk Skin Tone-scale targets (10 tones) and supplement chart testing with real subjects; note the finding that ISP/processing stage critically affects color error for darker tones (tone 7–10 error rises with exposure) [30] [31]. ΔE + Individual Typology Angle (ITA) is the current standard for skin-tone fidelity/bias pipelines, with consistently higher errors reported for darker skin [32].
- **Portrait-specific evaluation:** PPR10K contributes human-region-weighted (HRP) objective measures and group-level consistency checks — adopt these metrics for portrait mode [15].
- **Night / sunset intent:** the EHNQ database (1,500 enhanced night images from 100 sources × 15 algorithms, with subjective scores) and the BEHN blind index target exactly the failure modes that destroy night intent: inappropriate brightness/contrast, deformed structure, and **unnatural colorfulness** — use BEHN/EHNQ-style checks so "enhancement" doesn't turn a night scene into day or oversaturate a sunset [21]. SIDD's per-scene lighting condition labels (low/normal/high, illuminant temperature in the directory names) give a ready-made stratification for low-light test slices [19].

**Evaluation plan (proposal):** fixed holdout of user-licensed RAWs stratified by skin tone × scene illuminance; report skin-ROI ΔE00 (signed Δa*), ITA, BEHN-style night indices, KonCept512, PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, plus a small human preference study (2AFC bracket protocol as in the Imatest validation) — and only then any comparative claim vs. Lightroom outputs processed through the same RAW decode.

---

## 5. RAW color management and low-memory processing

- **rawpy/LibRaw (MIT / LGPL-2.1):** 16-bit linear output via `raw.postprocess(gamma=(1,1), no_auto_bright=True, output_bps=16)` — the direct replacement for 8-bit Pillow RGB [12]. Wheels bundle the LCMS color engine and DNG codecs but **exclude the GPL demosaic packs** (license-incompatible with MIT), so demosaicing is limited to LibRaw's default unless you build from source or add a separate (e.g., commercial) demosaicer [10] [11]. Camera coverage follows LibRaw; very new bodies may be unsupported until LibRaw updates, and exotic formats may need DNG conversion [11].
- **Production footgun:** Linux wheels enable OpenMP, which deadlocks with `multiprocessing` `fork` — use `spawn`/`forkserver` in the FastAPI worker setup [10].
- **Pipeline design (proposal grounded in the HDR+/rawpy evidence):** RAW → rawpy 16-bit linear (black-level subtract, WB gains, demosaic, lens-shading) → scene-linear working space (the HDR+ DNG sidecar documents exactly these color fields: AsShotNeutral, ColorMatrix{1,2}, CalibrationIlluminant{1,2}, Black/WhiteLevel) [18] → learned edit (3D LUT / bilateral grid, possibly on a downscale with parameter transfer) → display transform with 16-bit pipeline throughout; keep HDRNet's lesson that its HDR+-trained model expects 16-bit linear input and produces "uncanny colors" on sRGB input [5].
- **Low-memory execution:** tile with ≥10% overlap, 8/64-px dimension alignment, float32/float16/bfloat16, and Gaussian/multi-band blending with per-tile histogram matching; merge in image space [27]. NILUT-style implicit LUTs are "very compact in comparison to complete 3D LUTs" and its deployed-style global operator fits a 35 KB TFLite model with ~2×10⁻⁷ max error — an argument for parameter-transfer over pixel-tiles wherever the operator is global [4] [26].

---

## 6. Sequencing (proposal)

1. **Weeks 1–2 — RAW foundation:** rawpy 16-bit linear decode + LCMS-managed working space; kill the 8-bit Pillow path; add `spawn`-based workers. Validate color against a ColorChecker/Monk-scale chart (ΔE00 thresholds of §4) [10] [30].
2. **Weeks 3–6 — LUT engine:** integrate Image-Adaptive-3DLUT (Apache-2.0) with identity-LUT passthrough and user-installable .cube support; add NILUT fitting for style packs (code MIT, but source your own LUTs) [1] [3].
3. **Weeks 5–10 — Training data:** secure rights: commission expert retouching pairs and/or negotiate Adobe FiveK permission; build an internal PPR10K-style pipeline (HRP + GLC recipes, XMP targets) on your own licensed portraits; use FiveK/PPR10K strictly as research/eval references [13] [16].
4. **Weeks 8–14 — Learned model:** train the adaptive-LUT/conditional-bilateral model on your licensed pairs; verify 480p→4K parameter transfer on a full-res holdout; add skin-stratified ΔE00 and night-intent checks to CI [1] [26].
5. **Later — optional restoration opt-ins:** NAFNet-SIDD denoise and Real-ESRGAN upscale behind explicit user consent, with per-scene/skin-tone QA before enabling defaults; HDRNet-style spatial adaptation only if the global operator demonstrably under-fits [9] [8] [5].

## 7. What is *not* established (do not claim)
- No reviewed source demonstrates parity with Adobe Lightroom on matched inputs; LUT/HDRNet papers compare against FiveK/PPR10K metrics (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/MSE) or claim SOTA within their own benchmark family, not against Lightroom [6] [2] [25].
- Full-resolution consistency is *reported* only for global/low-capacity operators (3D LUTs, HDRNet with full-res loss); convolutional restorers still need tiles + blending, with seam risk the tiling references themselves acknowledge [1] [27].
- Commercial training on FiveK and PPR10K is prohibited by their current licenses; any architecture plan must assume replacement training data [13] [16].
